title: [P2] Classifier: stranger phrasings of seeded classes return unclassified — evidence-echo (top-3) would close the gap
detail: Dogfood match-sweep (2026-09-24, edeb898): canonical seed phrasings hit 6/6 at 0.90 signature; multi-line pasted log with the same vocabulary also 0.90; but stranger paraphrases of SEEDED classes returned unclassified 5/9 (missed: shared-checkout-collision, secret-env-clobber, disk-pressure-corruption, key-rotation-expiry, guard-degradation). Root causes, three distinct mechanisms: (a) keyword threshold 0.6 — 'two foremen committed to the same worktree checkout' hits only 2/6 shared-checkout-collision keywords, below the gate, even though the class is about exactly this; (b) inflection — 'lost the API key' vs keyword 'secrets', 'duckdb file corruption' vs 'corrupt' (substring, so 'corruption' DOES hit — the real miss there was 'disk full' vs 'disk pressure' + signature window; 'git push 403' has keyword 401 present but only 1/6); (c) signature regex windows (.{0,40}/.{0,60}) too narrow for real sentence shapes. The honest refusal is by design (LORE doctrine) — the gap is that the user gets NO graded signal: classify_all() already computes below-threshold scores and throws them away. Fix direction: an --explain/evidence-echo mode (or a 'near-misses' section in match output) that prints the top-3 below-threshold candidates with their keyword scores — e.g. 'shared-checkout-collision score 0.33 (2/6: worktree, collision)'. Registry stays closed; nothing is auto-labeled; the operator SEES which curated class was nearly named and can phrase the symptom its way. Also file the one defect-class gap: there is NO class for 'banned command tripped the gateway guard' (guard-degradation's signatures are strictly about worktree-vs-main gate equivalence). Evidence: commands and outputs in docs/dogfood/2026-09-24-integration.md.
